title: on-call-charter template variables
description: Values for templates/on-call-charter.md.j2 and templates/on-call-charter.html.j2. Generated by tpl-jinja from on-call-charter.md; `description` on each property is the question put to the author.

effective_date.title: Effective date
effective_date.description: The date this charter takes effect, ISO. On-call terms change what people are paid and when they sleep; an undated charter cannot be shown to have been agreed before the shift.

participants.title: Participants
participants.description: Everyone in the rotation, comma-separated. Count them: below five people, a weekly rotation means one week in four and this charter is a plan for attrition, not for coverage.

rotation_owner.title: Rotation owner
rotation_owner.description: The engineer who owns the schedule itself - swaps, gaps, escalation config. Not the manager. This role rotates yearly and the name here is who to chase when the calendar is empty.

schedule_repo_path.title: Schedule repo path
schedule_repo_path.description: Where the schedule config lives in version control. A rotation that exists only in a vendor UI has no review, no history and no answer to "who changed the escalation path".

shift_length.title: Shift length
shift_length.description: Length of one shift. 168h (a week) is the default for teams of 6 or more; anything shorter multiplies hand-offs, and a hand-off is where an unresolved incident gets forgotten.

team_name.description: The team that carries this pager, as the org chart names it. One team per charter - a shared rotation with two charters is how a page ends up acknowledged by nobody.

url.title: Url
url.description: Link to the written compensation policy. If it does not exist yet, write it before this charter ships - unpaid off-hours pages are the term people accept quietly and leave over.
